scenes.heading: Solving linear inequalities
scenes.sub: Not one answer, a whole range
scenes.say: How many rides can Ava afford? What heights are allowed on the roller coaster? These questions have a whole range of answers. That's what inequalities are for.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: "At least 120 cm tall" allows every height from 120 cm up
scenes.science: x ≥ 3 includes 3 and every number above it
scenes.breaks: heights can't be negative, but x can be any number, including negatives and fractions.
scenes.say: A sign saying you must be at least one hundred and twenty centimetres tall doesn't describe one height. It allows every height from one hundred and twenty up, including one hundred and twenty itself. An inequality is a rule that a whole range of numbers can pass.
scenes.caption: A sign saying you must be at least 120 cm tall allows every height from 120 cm up, including 120 itself. An inequality is a rule that a whole range of numbers can pass.

scenes.heading: Showing x > 3
scenes.say: Solve four x minus three is greater than nine: add three, divide by four, and x is greater than three. First the number line, then an open circle at three, because three itself is not included, then an arrow to the right.
scenes.caption: Solve 4x − 3 > 9: add 3, divide by 4, and x > 3. An open circle at 3, because 3 is not included, then an arrow to the right.

scenes.heading: The one new rule
scenes.say: Two is less than five. Multiply both by negative one: negative two is greater than negative five. The order swapped. So when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative, reverse the sign. Adding and subtracting never reverse it.
scenes.caption: 2 < 5. Multiply both by −1: −2 > −5. The order swapped. So when you multiply or divide both sides by a negative, reverse the sign. Adding and subtracting never reverse it.

scenes.heading: Dividing by a negative
scenes.question: Solve 5 − 3x ≥ 17.
scenes.say: Solve five minus three x is at least seventeen. Subtract five: negative three x is at least twelve. Divide by negative three, and flip the sign: x is less than or equal to negative four. Test negative five: twenty is at least seventeen.
scenes.caption: Solve 5 − 3x ≥ 17. Subtract 5: −3x ≥ 12. Divide by −3, and flip the sign: x ≤ −4. Test −5: 20 ≥ 17.

scenes.heading: A double inequality
notes: Subtract 1, divide by 2: all three parts
scenes.say: Solve negative three is less than two x plus one, which is at most seven. Do every step to all three parts: subtract one, then divide by two. Negative two is less than x, which is at most three. On the line: an open circle at negative two, a closed circle at three, and a bar between.
scenes.caption: Solve −3 < 2x + 1 ≤ 7. Do every step to all three parts: subtract 1, then divide by 2. −2 < x ≤ 3. Open circle at −2, closed circle at 3, and a bar between.

scenes.heading: How many rides?
scenes.question: Ava has $50, spent $14 on a ticket, and rides cost $4.50. How many rides?
scenes.say: Ava has fifty dollars, has spent fourteen on a ticket, and rides cost four dollars fifty. Fourteen plus four point five r is at most fifty. Subtract fourteen, divide by four point five: r is at most eight. Eight rides.
scenes.caption: Ava has $50, has spent $14, and rides cost $4.50. 14 + 4.5r ≤ 50. Subtract 14, divide by 4.5: r ≤ 8. Eight rides.

points: × or ÷ by a negative: flip the sign
Test a number inside and outside
scenes.say: Quick recap. Solve like an equation. Multiply or divide by a negative, flip the sign. Open circles for less than and greater than, closed circles when the number is included. Change all three parts of a double inequality. Now try the practice questions!
